categories.main_business_segments: Shima Seiki's primary business segments are: (1) Flat knitting machines, (2) Design systems, (3) Glove and sock knitting machines, and (4) Other related services and parts. The company also engages in the manufacturing and sales of related components and provides maintenance and other services.
categories.core_technologies_production_methods: The company is a global leader in computerized flat knitting machines, including its proprietary WHOLEGARMENT technology for seamless knitwear production. It also develops advanced design systems (SDS-ONE APEX series) and automated cutting machines (P-CAM series), integrating IT, AI, and digitalization to support end-to-end apparel production. Manufacturing is highly integrated, with most production centralized in Wakayama, Japan, and some parts outsourced to subsidiaries.
categories.primary_customers_markets: Shima Seiki primarily serves apparel and fashion industry manufacturers, especially knitwear producers, as well as glove and sock manufacturers. Its customer base includes global apparel brands, knitwear factories, and increasingly, non-apparel sectors such as sports, medical, interior, and industrial materials.
categories.geographic_coverage: The company operates globally, with major sales in Asia (notably China, ASEAN, Bangladesh), Europe (especially Italy), the Middle East (notably Turkey), and Japan. Overseas sales account for approximately 80% of total revenue, supported by subsidiaries and distributors in Europe, the Americas, Greater China, Southeast Asia, and Korea.
categories.supply_chain_position: Shima Seiki is positioned as an upstream to midstream supplier, providing essential production equipment (knitting machines, design systems, cutting machines) and solutions to manufacturers in the textile and apparel value chain. It enables efficient, on-demand, and sustainable production for downstream apparel brands and factories.
categories.strategic_focus_rd_direction: Strategic priorities include rebuilding the business foundation, establishing solution-based business models, revitalizing the flat knitting machine segment, and expanding the automated cutting machine business. R&D focuses on sustainable manufacturing, digital transformation (DX) of the apparel supply chain, AI-driven design systems, and developing new applications for non-apparel markets. The company is also investing in decarbonization, human capital, and cost reduction.
categories.revenue_model: Revenue is primarily generated through the sale of capital equipment (knitting machines, design systems, cutting machines), software licensing (including subscription-based models for design software), parts, and maintenance services. Some recurring revenue is derived from software subscriptions and after-sales support.
categories.key_competitors_industry_positioning: Key competitors include other global knitting machine manufacturers, particularly from China and Europe. Shima Seiki is recognized as a technology leader and innovator, especially in seamless knitting (WHOLEGARMENT) and integrated digital solutions, but faces increasing price and technology competition, especially from Chinese firms.
categories.financial_scale_growth_profile: In FY2025, consolidated sales were 32.5 billion yen, with a net loss of 14.3 billion yen, reflecting a significant downturn from the previous year due to weak global demand and inventory write-downs. The company has a strong equity ratio (78.2%) and aims for a recovery and growth to 55 billion yen in sales and 5.5 billion yen in net profit by FY2027 under its mid-term plan, but is currently in a contraction phase.
categories.value_proposition_product_differentiatio: Shima Seiki differentiates itself through advanced, integrated solutions that enable on-demand, sustainable, and highly efficient knitwear production, including seamless WHOLEGARMENT technology. Its unique value lies in supporting the entire apparel supply chain with digitalization, rapid prototyping, and environmentally conscious manufacturing, helping customers reduce lead times, waste, and costs while enabling creative design.
